hints.content: Note that the graph of $h$ can be obtained by transforming the graph of $g$, since $h(x)=g(x+2)+3$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Given that $g(x)=-|x|$, we have the following:

>$\begin{align}g(x)&=-|x|\\\\
g(x+2)&=-|x+2|\\\\
g(x+2)+3&=-|x+2|+3
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $h(x)$.  Therefore, $h(x)=g(x+2)+3$.

hints.content:
- Replacing $x$ with $x+ 2$ shifts the graph of $g$ to the left by $2$ units.

- Adding $3$ to the function shifts the graph of $g$ up by $3$ units.

Therefore, *the graph of $h$ is obtained by shifting the graph of $g$ to the left by $2$ units and up by $3$ units.*
